I reported abuse.
I was ignored.
I lost my business, my

safety, and almost my life

— while the people meant to

protect me watched.

They said I was paranoid.
They told me to go to the police.
I’d told them about the police.
And when I try and explain?
People stop replying, what I have

been through, is not normal.

This site holds every ignored call,

redacted record, and unanswered warning.
 It names every person who had

a chance to help — and didn’t.

You are now a witness of the

#TheUndercoverVictim.

Thank you for taking the time to come here,

for me this is everything, nothing will ever be the same

But at least I can explain why....

Police Please • Evidence Vault

The Leadership Vacuum — “Holiday Alibi”

🗓️ 17 Apr 2025 • 04:42 🚔 Sussex Police Contradiction • High

“17 Days Without a Supervisor”

Each one is real. Documented. Ignored. #Victim #Erasure #YouAreAWitness #TheUndercoverVictim

🎥 Don’t Kill People • #circles

🎥 “You wouldn’t go narrow-boating on your own, would you?”

What this proves

At 04:42 on 17 April 2025, Sussex Police confirmed my entire chain — Dixon, Duffy, Palmer — was on leave at the same time. My suicide disclosure from 6 April was only logged on the 17th. This isn’t clerical error; it’s proof of a leadership vacuum that left a stalking victim without safeguarding.

  • Contradictions: July vs November mismatch • Chain-on-leave • Suicide-log delay • Contact centre barrier.
  • Laws engaged: Victims’ Code (updates, continuity) • ECHR Art.2 (right to life duties) • DPA 2018/UK GDPR (record accuracy, access).
📖 Click here for the full Section 3.3 narrative

The Leadership Vacuum & Culture of Complicity

These failures aren’t isolated errors. They flow from a strategic leadership vacuum in Sussex Police. A culture of complicity prioritised reputation over safeguarding, creating a “bullshit machine” where accountability was impossible.

Psychology of Complicity

Officers displaced responsibility upwards, silencing conscience. Good people did nothing — and harm was normalised.

The Scapegoat Protocol

PC Dixon was made the sole point of failure, shielding senior command. If pressure grew, he could be sacrificed while systemic rot persisted.

The Holiday Alibi

After my 6 April suicide disclosure, the entire chain vanished on leave for 17 days. The disclosure was logged only on the 17th. No oversight, no handover — organised abandonment.

Demands
  • Identify the senior officer(s) in command 6–23 April 2025.
  • Audit why all supervisors were absent without handover.
  • Investigate misuse of GDPR and leave rotas as shields.

The real failure is not at the bottom of this hierarchy. It is in the silence at the top.

“NARROWBOATING INVESTIGATION” — because apparently, supervision is seasonal.

#PolicePlease #DeathBySilence #HolidayAlibi #UndercoverVictim

📖 Narrative — The Humiliation Protocol (22 Jun 2025)

The Humiliation Protocol

On June 22, 2025, I made a 25-minute call to the Sussex Police 101 service that I can only describe as a harrowing and humiliating experience. It came after I had already been hung up on four times while trying to report new criminal behaviour from my abuser, Alanna O'Hare. The entire call was a live-recorded example of institutional gaslighting.

My Suicide Attempt Was Questioned
When I tried to explain the urgency of my situation, I told the handler that my officer, PC Dixon, had not contacted me since April 6th, clarifying, "That was the day of my suicide". The handler's response was shocking. He said, "What do you mean? You're talking to me now. So you're not Dead. Are you?". I had to explain that I survived it. It was a moment of profound humiliation, and I told him, "I'm not a ghost. That was insulting".

My Rights and Evidence Were Dismissed
Throughout the call, I felt my rights as a victim were systematically denied and my attempts to provide new evidence were obstructed.

  • Victim's Code Breach: I specifically requested a call back "under the victim's code". The handler told me, "You don't get to quote that, and then you... You get exactly what you want". I had to correct him, stating, "As a victim, my love, you do".
  • Obstruction of Evidence: I was trying to report that my abuser had called and messaged me five times and falsely accused me of rape. Instead of being allowed to log a new crime, I was told it would not be treated as such and that a previously scheduled video interview had been denied.
  • Misuse of GDPR: I asked if my abuser was on bail, which is my right to know under the Victim's Code. The handler refused to tell me, incorrectly citing GDPR. I argued that this wasn't a GDPR issue but a Sussex Police policy used to obscure information.
  • Safeguarding Failure: I stated clearly, "I've called 45 times since April 6th and I have not had a call back". No officer had contacted me since my suicide attempt. There was also significant confusion about my case; the handler gave me a crime reference number (47240141246) and first said no officer was assigned, before later confirming it was PC Dixon—the very officer I had said was under an IOPC investigation.

At the end of the call, I was emotionally exhausted. I expressed my feeling that "Sussex Police don't think I matter". After 45 unanswered calls since my suicide attempt, I told the handler, "I’d say I was getting erased". The call is the audio record of a system that, in my view, has chosen to protect itself by erasing those it has failed.

📖 Narrative — Section 3.48: The Retaliatory Hang-Up Calls (22 Jun 2025)

The Retaliatory Hang-Up Calls

This analysis covers two brief but damning 101 calls that occurred at 04:56 and 05:00 on June 22, 2025, just minutes after the "Humiliation Protocol" call was terminated. These recordings provide proof of a coordinated and retaliatory refusal of service.

The Incidents
In both calls, after navigating the automated system, I was connected to a live operator. The moment I began to speak, the line was terminated, confirmed by the audible "beep beep beep" of a disconnected call. The second of these calls is particularly clear evidence, as I state my purpose is to report being hung up on, only to be hung up on again.

The Context is Everything
These were not random technical faults. Coming immediately after I had directly confronted the police with evidence of their cover-up, these hang-ups can only be interpreted as deliberate acts. They suggest that my phone number or identity had been flagged within their system, and that call handlers were now under instruction not to engage with me.

Constructive Refusal of Service
This pattern constitutes a constructive refusal of service. By repeatedly terminating calls from a known victim of crime, Sussex Police were actively denying me my right to report incidents, seek updates, or access the services they are legally obligated to provide. This is a severe breach of the Victims' Code and a dereliction of their fundamental duties.

Retaliation Against a Whistleblower
This is a clear act of retaliation. Having been exposed in the previous call, the system's response was not to address the issue, but to silence the person who had exposed it. This is a punitive measure taken against a victim for having the audacity to hold the institution to account.

Conclusion
These recordings are short, but their implications are profound. They are the sound of a system closing its doors on a victim it has deemed problematic. They prove that the issues I faced were not due to the actions of a single officer, but were part of a coordinated, institutional strategy of silencing and obstruction. This is not just poor service; it is a calculated act of retaliation that must be investigated as a serious form of police misconduct.

Cherish These Moments, Ben

22 June 2025

And when the sun goes
over the same skyline —
down on the victim,
down with the 101 callers,
down with the police.

A day of going round in circles.

This is my life.
This is purpose.
Warped. Surreal. Content.

Cherish these moments, Ben.
